Hi Samira — thanks for the workbook and for the time earlier. I'm looping in Kar (pricing) and Grace (solutions) so we can get you a written comparison and a proposed commercial that addresses both upfront cash concerns and operational risk.

Quick answers up front:
- We can structure a price-match + migration credit (one-time credit tied to invoices) that offsets your first 3–6 months of delta; exact sizing depends on the procurement levers you can accept (prepay vs credits, committed MRR, term).
- Seat -> hybrid packaging is reasonable; we usually model a base-seat minimum + a lower per-token overage (consumption) to preserve predictable revenue while giving flexibility.
- Runtime: our main customer considerations are prefix caching behavior during rollout, KV cache warmup for long-chat sessions, and quantization differences on small-batch low-latency tails. We include a staged canary with prefix-preserving caches and a fallback to a verified compatible variant to avoid quality cliffs.

Can Kar and Grace outline two concrete commercial options (price-match + migration-credit; and accelerated prepay bundle with onboarding credits) plus a short ops runbook for a low-risk cutover? Samira, can you confirm if Procurement wants credits applied as invoice credits or applied to a committed prepay bucket?

I'll produce a short one-pager for Monday once we have Kar's numbers.

—Dylan

Samira and team — apologies for the quick turnaround but attached below are two options and a short ops summary. I'm pasting the high-level snapshots here so Procurement can start review.

Option A — Price-match + migration credit (invoice credit)
- Price-match: Redwood will match incumbent effective unit economics for the first 6 months (rate-card parity).
- Migration credit: One-time credit equal to 60% of estimated migration uplift (applied as invoice credit across months 1–3).
- Term & commit: 12-month contract, no prepay required; tiered overage rate at 5% below incumbent after month 6 if commit renewed.
- Cash impact: zero net cash difference months 0–3; slightly positive for MerchantWay months 4–6 due to tiered overage buffer.
- Pros/cons: lowest procurement friction; requires clearer quality-run metrics to avoid open disputes on uplift sizing.

Option B — Accelerated prepay + onboarding credits (prepay bucket)
- Prepay: 3-month prepaid consumption bucket at a 6% discount to list.
- Onboarding credits: $X onboarding credit applied to Redwood professional services and dedicated ramp (applied up-front to invoices).
- Migration credit: additional performance escrow for rollback (held for 90 days, refundable if SLAs not met).
- Cash impact: MerchantWay pays up-front for 3 months (negative near-term cash), but total 12-month TCO can be 3–5% lower depending on utilization.
- Pros/cons: better unit economics if MerchantWay can accept up-front; stronger operational commitment.

Ops summary (Grace) — key runbook bullets:
- Canary: Start with 5% traffic, preserve prefix caching for top 50 endpoints, route long-tail (>2048 tokens) to incumbent for first 2 weeks.
- KV cache warmup: pre-seed KV caches for active sessions during a staged cutover window; expect 15–30% higher tail latency on cold-start sessions without pre-seeding.
- Quantization: suggest INT8 profile for most paths; keep FP16 variant available for high-fidelity long-chat endpoints during first 30 days.
- Billing packaging: map seats to a base-seat minimum; token consumption will bill to the prepay bucket or invoice for overages depending on chosen option.

Attachments included: merchantway_econ.xlsx (their workbook, annotated) and a short commercial summary PDF.

Samira — which option does Procurement prefer as a starting point? If A, we'll provide the invoice credit contract language and a short SOW for the ramp. If B, we'll send a draft prepay amendment and the escrow terms to legal.
